mechanism_narrative: The continued week-by-week recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals more commuting and foot traffic, which should lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as people combine work trips with shopping and dining.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -64.0 to -54.1 and TRANSIT from -74.3 to -66.9 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days despite further weekly improvement in WORKPLACES or TRANSIT, or it falls below the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A still-elevated RESIDENTIAL index indicates more time spent at home, but the recent decline from 23.3 to 19.4 suggests people are resuming out-of-home activity; that shift should produce a one- to two-week lagged increase in RETAIL_REC as home time releases into discretionary trips.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays flat or rises while RETAIL_REC still increases, or if RETAIL_REC remains below its last 28-day mean after two weeks, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT remains below -65 and WORKPLACES remains below -50, the area is still operating under strong mobility constraints; in that regime retail visits continue to be suppressed, so RETAIL_REC should stay lower over the next month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -65 and WORKPLACES stays below -50 for at least 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -66.9 and WORKPLACES is -54.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain below the stated thresholds yet RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp recovery in PARKS use relative to the prior week marks warmer-weather leisure activity and spillover to nearby discretionary shopping; that seasonal leisure shift should push RETAIL_REC upward within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by at least 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -37.3 to -29.6 in the latest week
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week, the claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS both recover together, households are already making more essential and leisure trips, which increases the probability of additional retail stops and raises RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -39.1 to -32.0 and PARKS from -43.7 to -29.6 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS continue improving but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last 28-day average within two weeks, the mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A plateau in WORKPLACES recovery after a strong rebound signals that commuting demand is nearing a ceiling; once that plateau is reached, the retail rebound slows and RETAIL_REC turns lower relative to the last month over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stays within 2 points of its current level for 2 straight weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved steadily but remains deeply negative at -54.1
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES plateaus near its current level yet RETAIL_REC rises over the following month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM implies broader reopening of travel and daily errands; if that joint recovery continues, RETAIL_REC should rise after a one- to two-week lag as shopping trips resume.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -74.3 to -66.9 while GROCERY_PHARM improved from -39.1 to -32.0
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and GROCERY_PHARM keep improving but RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines over the next two weeks, the claim fails.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL falls while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue rising, then trips are shifting away from staying at home toward outside activity; this mobility reallocation should increase RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines for 2 consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 23.3 to 19.4 while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT also improved
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL declines alongside rising WORKPLACES and TRANSIT but RETAIL_REC does not move above its last 28-day mean within four weeks, the hypothesis is rejected.
